page.layout: One printed page, right side of the scan. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Text block in one column with a display formula in the middle. Right margin carries only handwritten annotations, which are not transcribed. The left edge shows the neighbouring page and is excluded.

main_text.l: Quanquam plures sunt additionis compositiones, qualis est σὼ θροις λόγος [?],
ad 1 5 d. 5: inter eas tamen haec maxime frequens est, quare specialis haec definitio huic
instituto sufficiens, generalis loco assumpta sit. Exempli
gratia, si 3 ad 2 sunt, ut 9 ad 6: tum per additionis com-
positionem 3 & 9, id est 12, ad 2 & 6, id est 8, pariter se
habebunt, sesquialtera nempe ratione. Unde termini pro-

l.i: Si e terminus multiplicis proportionis unius ra-
parati dentur: tum ut antecedentes per additionem
compositi ad consequentes additos sunt, ita & sing-
uli antecedentes ad suos sigillatim consequentes

main_text.l: Est 12 p. 7, nisi quòd inuersè & huic proposito ac-
commodatius paulò enunciata est. Asserit enim illa, Datis
quotlibet numeris proportionalibus: quantus sit unus
antecedens ad suum consequentem, tantos fore omnes

page.notes: Handwritten annotations in the right margin and at the foot of the page (including the marginal Theorema notes and the lines beginning "Regula") are manuscript and were not transcribed. The Greek word in the second paragraph is uncertain. The last printed line is partly overwritten by handwriting. Section symbols and superscript numbers in the display formula are as far as I could read them.
